description: Indirect heat raised in a boiler or CHP unit and distributed as steam or hot water. One branch, not tiered (design doc D3); steam conditions ride as temperature-output and pressure-output. CHP sits here with electricity as a secondary output (D1).
Direct heat delivered between 150 and 400 degC.
Moisture removal and thermal separation. Kept distinct from process heat because both sources treat it as its own service and non-thermal routes compete here.
Upstream conditioning of feed: sintering, pelletising, coke making, crushing and grinding.
The chemical or metallurgical transformation at the core of the sector: reduction, calcination, cracking, reforming, pulping, smelting.
Casting, rolling, drawing, sheet forming, coating and finishing.
Motors, pumps, fans, compressors and conveying.
Space conditioning, lighting and other non-process site energy use.
Residual energy service, for balancing a sector's energy total. Should shrink as coverage grows.
